added_lemmas.statement:
For every \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\), suppose that no summary bidirected edge joins \(Y\) to a component label \(B\) that is either \(Y\) itself or has a directed path to \(Y\) in \(\mathcal S\). Then, without requiring the strongly connected component of \(Y\) in \(\mathcal S\) to be a singleton,
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal M}[Y_0\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x,Z=z)]
=\mathbb E_p[Y_0\mid X_{-\gamma}=x,Z=z],\qquad x\in\{0,1\},
\]
and consequently \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
W=\operatorname{PP}_{\mathcal S,L}(Y_0)
=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z,
\qquad w_x=(x,z),\quad x\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The disjoint union in (1) follows from \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\) and the definition of \(Z\). By \(\text{ass:strict-observed-positivity}\), every full-window cell has positive \(p\)-mass. Each assignment \(W=w_x\) has at least one extension to \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\), and its probability is the sum of the positive probabilities of all such extensions. Hence
\[
p(W=w_x)>0,\qquad x\in\{0,1\},
\tag{2}
\]
so both observational conditional expectations in the statement are defined.

We first locate the actual parents of the terminal vertex. If \((B,s)\in\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)\), then \((B,s)\to(Y,0)\in E_G^{\to}\). Membership of \(G\) in \(\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\), together with \(\text{ass:positive-bounded-directed-lags}\), gives
\[
1\le -s\le L.
\tag{3}
\]
The exact projection condition \(\text{ass:exact-summary-projection}\) gives \(B\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\). Equations (3) and the definition of the positive-lag possible-parent set therefore imply
\[
\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)\subseteq W.
\tag{4}
\]
The same positive-lag condition also makes \(Y_0\) terminal in the observed window: an edge \(Y_0\to(C,t)\) would require \(t\ge1\), whereas every \(t\in\mathbb T_H\) satisfies \(t\le0\).

Let \(\mathcal E_Y\) be the set of exogenous-factor indices consisting of the private index \(\{Y_0\}\) and every bidirected-edge index incident to \(Y_0\). We claim that none of the factors \((U_a:a\in\mathcal E_Y)\) occurs in the recursive determination of \(V_W\). Indeed, acyclicity of the ADMG and \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\) imply, by induction along a topological ordering of \(E_G^{\to}\), that every coordinate of \(V_W\) is a deterministic function only of exogenous factors incident to its directed ancestors. The private factor of \(Y_0\) could reach \(W\) only along a directed path beginning at \(Y_0\), which is impossible because \(Y_0\) is terminal. Now consider an incident pairwise factor with edge
\[
Y_0\leftrightarrow(B,s).
\tag{5}
\]
If this factor occurred in the recursion for a coordinate \((C,-\ell)\in W\), then terminality again excludes the route starting at \(Y_0\); therefore \((B,s)\) would have a directed path in \(G\) to \((C,-\ell)\). Projecting the edges on this path gives a directed walk from \(B\) to \(C\) in \(\mathcal S\). Since \((C,-\ell)\in W\), the definition of \(W\) gives \(C\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\). Deleting repetitions from the concatenated directed walk shows that \(B\) is a directed ancestor of \(Y\), with the reflexive case \(B=Y\) included. But (5) projects to \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), contradicting the graphical premise. This proves the claim.

Let \(\mathcal E_W\) denote the exogenous-factor indices occurring in the recursive determination of \(V_W\). The preceding paragraph proves \(\mathcal E_Y\cap\mathcal E_W=\varnothing\). By \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\), the finite family of all private and pairwise factors is mutually independent. Direct factorization of its finite joint mass function therefore gives
\[
(U_a:a\in\mathcal E_Y)\mathbin{\perp}V_W.
\tag{6}
\]
This argument permits different pairwise latent factors to overlap at an observed vertex; it uses only that the factors indexed by distinct private vertices or bidirected edges are independent.

Write \(U_Y=(U_a:a\in\mathcal E_Y)\). By \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\) and (4), there is a deterministic binary table, namely the frozen structural table at \(Y_0\), such that
\[
Y_0=f_{Y_0}(V_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},U_Y).
\tag{7}
\]
For either \(x\in\{0,1\}\), equations (2), (6), and (7) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_p[Y_0\mid W=w_x]
&=\sum_u f_{Y_0}((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u)
   \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u\mid W=w_x)\\
&=\sum_u f_{Y_0}((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u)
   \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Here the first equality also uses \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\), which identifies the observational law of \(\mathcal M\) with \(p\). Under \(\operatorname{do}(W=w_x)\), every actual parent in (4) is fixed to its corresponding entry of \(w_x\), while an intervention leaves the exogenous distribution unchanged. The truncated structural recursion and (7) thus give
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal M}[Y_0\mid\operatorname{do}(W=w_x)]
=\sum_u f_{Y_0}((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u)
   \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u).
\tag{9}
\]
Comparing (8) and (9), and then using (1), proves the two displayed equalities in the statement. Subtracting the case \(x=0\) from the case \(x=1\) and applying \(\text{def:micro-cde}\) and the definition of \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\) proves \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\).

The removed singleton-SCC premise is genuinely unnecessary in this positive-lag setting. For an exact four-vertex check, take \(\mathcal V=\{X,Y\}\), \(H=L=\gamma=1\), directed edges \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(Y_{-1}\to X_0\), no bidirected edges, mutually independent nondegenerate private bits, and \(Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin{\oplus}E_Y\) with \(\Pr(E_Y=1)=\delta\in(0,1/2)\). The summary has the directed cycle \(X\to Y\to X\), every observed cell can be made positive, and both the interventional and conditional contrasts equal \(1-2\delta\).

The no-bidirected-ancestor premise is load-bearing. Retain \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\), add \(X_{-1}\leftrightarrow Y_0\), let the shared edge latent \(U\) be fair, and take independent noises \(E_X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e)\) and \(E_Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\delta)\), where \(e,\delta\in(0,1/2)\). Set
\[
X_{-1}=U\mathbin{\oplus}E_X,
\qquad
Y_0=(X_{-1}\mathbin{\lor}U)\mathbin{\oplus}E_Y,
\tag{10}
\]
and let the other two window variables be independent nondegenerate private bits. All sixteen observed cells are positive. Direct calculation gives
\[
q(\mathcal M)=\frac{1-2\delta}{2},
\qquad
\mathbb E[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=1]-\mathbb E[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=0]
=(1-2\delta)(1-e),
\tag{11}
\]
which are unequal because \(e\ne1/2\). Thus removing the bidirected-ancestor condition would make the conclusion false.
added_lemmas.justification: Strict positive directed lags make the end-of-window outcome terminal and place all of its actual observed parents inside the controlled possible-parent vector.
added_lemmas.gap: The published adjustment result retains a singleton strongly connected component condition; this direct semi-Markovian argument removes it within the paper's finite-window binary independent-edge-latent model.
added_lemmas.consumer: The strengthened collapse theorem uses this lemma to identify the common micro controlled direct effect even when the summary graph has directed cycles through \(Y\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\ne\varnothing\) and no summary bidirected edge joins \(Y\) to a component label that is either \(Y\) itself or has a directed path to \(Y\) in \(\mathcal S\). Then every \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\) satisfies \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\), and
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\},
\qquad
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\]
In particular, the conclusion permits directed cycles through \(Y\) in the summary graph; the positive-lag unrolling, not a singleton strongly connected component, supplies the terminal-time argument.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Strict observed positivity and \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\) ensure that both events \(\{X_{-\gamma}=x,Z=z\}\), \(x\in\{0,1\}\), have positive \(p\)-probability, as proved in equations (1)--(2) of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\). Hence \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\) is well defined.

Fix an arbitrary \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\). The graphical premise of the present theorem is exactly the graphical premise of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\); all of that lemma's structural and compatibility hypotheses follow from membership in the fiber and the listed assumptions. Therefore
\[
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{12}
\]
Because the chosen member was arbitrary, the definition of the attainable set gives
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\subseteq\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{13}
\]
The nonempty-fiber premise supplies at least one pair \((G,\mathcal M)\) in the fiber, and (12) shows that this pair attains \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\). Thus the reverse inclusion in (13) holds and
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{14}
\]
Finally, by \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\), \(\underline q(p)\) and \(\overline q(p)\) are respectively the infimum and supremum of the set in (14). The infimum and supremum of a nonempty singleton equal its unique element, proving
\[
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\]
No step uses a singleton strongly connected component. The cyclic four-vertex model displayed in \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\) verifies directly that the enlarged graphical regime is nonempty and can have a summary cycle through \(Y\).
added_lemmas.justification: The sharp refinement envelope should expose every point-identified face justified by the positive-lag structure, including summaries with directed cycles through the outcome label.
added_lemmas.gap: Within the finite-window binary independent-pairwise-latent class, positive lags remove the singleton-SCC premise from the analogous Ferreira--Assaad adjustment regime; endpoint collapse over the refinement union is new.
added_lemmas.consumer: Applied users obtain the adjustment contrast whenever the bidirected-ancestor exclusion holds, even if the summary directed graph is cyclic through \(Y\), and obtain the sharp envelope otherwise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The cited leaf includes a singleton-SCC premise and cannot carry the directive's broader positive-lag claim. It is replaced by a directly proved lemma that removes that premise while preserving the no-bidirected-ancestor condition.

The former theorem states only the narrower singleton-SCC collapse and frames it as recovery. Its proved successor permits directed summary cycles through the outcome label and records the strict positive-lag extension.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. Directed effects occur only at positive lags through \(L\), while bidirected dependence may span any summary-compatible pair of time points in the observed \(H\)-window. The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained range of a finite union of raw semi-Markovian response-function polynomial programs, and a total exact certifier returns incompatibility certificates or isolated algebraic endpoints with attaining SCMs. Positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal, so controlling its full possible-parent set identifies the effect by the Ferreira--Assaad adjustment contrast whenever no summary bidirected edge joins \(Y\) to a directed ancestor of \(Y\), even when the summary has directed cycles through \(Y\). The envelope is strictly narrower on a relative-open temporal-instrument family than a complete temporal-order comparator. Simultaneous multinomial regions support tie-aware inference. Exact analysis of the response-signature quotient supplies a general factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, while an explicit edge-latent-chain certificate shows that unrestricted quotient-simplex masses can enlarge the independent-edge-latent image; the endpoint compiler therefore retains the raw product parameterization in general.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph adjustment results retain sufficient graphical conditions suited to models that may contain contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws; they do not isolate the stronger terminal-time implication available in the present positive-lag independent-edge-latent model. Existing automated bounds take one fixed graph, and unrestricted response-signature quotient simplexes need not preserve nonlinear independent-edge-latent product images.
project_justification.niche: The positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite and makes the end-of-window outcome terminal, while summary-compatible bidirected lags remain unrestricted inside the observed window. Binary canonical response functions turn each fixed-refinement image into a compact semialgebraic set, and the complete temporal-order common-latent model supplies a coherent graph-free outer comparator.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler and a total exact certifier; proves a strict positive-lag adjustment extension that permits directed summary cycles through the outcome label; and embeds every refinement into the complete order-only comparator. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening. One multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, the project proves exact factorized push-forward fidelity, gives a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, and exhibits an exact separating certificate showing why unrestricted quotient-simplex masses cannot replace the raw product parameterization in general.

prose_updates.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and adjustment expression. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, the strict positive-lag restriction makes \(Y_0\) terminal and removes their singleton strongly connected component requirement: the adjustment remains valid despite directed summary cycles through \(Y\), provided no summary bidirected edge joins \(Y\) to a directed ancestor of \(Y\). This is a positive-lag extension within the present model class, not a claim that the present scope contains theirs: Ferreira--Assaad permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, whereas this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes the independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) inform finite-window reasoning for known bounded-lag periodic ADMGs but are not the source of the present positive-lag restriction. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026) and Choe et al. (2026) motivate quotient programs over unrestricted signature masses. Here exact push-forward preserves the raw image only while the induced factorized quotient family is retained: the edge-latent-chain certificate proves that freeing quotient masses can enlarge the image. A finite factor-incidence sentence decides equality, lexicographic minimization gives a semialgebraic selector when equality holds, and the derived quotient-size bound closes the former size question. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply the exact-elimination and complexity ancestors. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) shows that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the present temporal micro-CDE strictness region. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact push-forward to response-signature equivalence classes preserves the raw image when the induced factorized quotient family is retained, but this operation alone does not reduce the latent product parameterization. The unrestricted branchwise quotient simplex is computationally smaller but is not sound in general: on the six-window-vertex edge-latent-chain instance it contains a rational point violating an observational independence polynomial that vanishes on the raw image. The exact factor-incidence test decides graph by graph whether the unrestricted quotient happens to be safe, and the canonical catalogue has a derived finite quotient-size bound. Consequently the certified endpoint compiler retains raw product weights unless that test succeeds; the remaining limitation is worst-case combinatorial size, not an unresolved fidelity or size claim.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window; Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag cyclic-summary adjustment theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates; nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved rather than left open: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and the edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program; under the no-bidirected-ancestor condition, positive-lag terminality further collapses the envelope to the adjustment contrast even when the summary has directed cycles through \(Y\).
